part: task-interval clock and motion-duplicate census (review R1 follow-up)

tolerances.belt_clock_min_comparisons: max(8, ceil(half the comparisons available at lag 0)) at every lag considered
tolerances.belt_clock_method: per source heel strike h (joint frame, 1-based): mean over frames h+15..h+29 of the mean of that side's HEE and TOE central-difference velocities (x 100 Hz, m/s); belt speed = |AP component|, AP axis = the axis with the largest median |window velocity|; marker frames h+14..h+30 must be finite, not (0,0,0) and not flagged 0; compared with cvel[h+22+lag-1] (0-based) for heel strikes inside a transition interval (label a* or d*) +-300 frames; error = median |difference|

source.sha256_note: Recorded by earlier receipts; size and mtime re-checked before and after, bytes not rehashed.

realignment_rule_for_counts: cutPoints moved into joint frames as cut - best_lag (cvel index = joint frame + lag); counts only, nothing is converted.

misaligned.reason: not evaluable: cvel or a heel/toe marker is missing
not evaluable: cvel or a heel/toe marker is missing

alignment.reason: not evaluable: cvel or a heel/toe marker is missing
not evaluable: cvel or a heel/toe marker is missing

limitations: Belt speed from heel/toe markers is an estimate; aligned controls show +10 to +17 frame lags, absorbed by the +-50 frame tolerance but not calibrated.
Duplicate detection is exact-byte only; near-copies are not detected.
Counts under re-alignment use one global lag per recording; drift within a recording is not tested.
